newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE says Bosnia presidency result likely Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Bosnia presidency result likely Tuesday.

text.p: International supervisors of Bosnia's countrywide elections said on Monday the results of the contest for a three-man national presidency would not be announced until Tuesday.
"It is now clear that the presidency count will not be established until tomorrow," Robert Frowick, head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE) mission in Bosnia, told reporters.

Frowick said the OSCE had hoped to announce the result of the vote for the collective presidency, on which the Serb, Croat and Moslem communities each have one seat, late on Monday, but the results were coming in more slowly than expected.
The presidency is the most closely watched contest.

Although the current Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic is certain of winning the Moslem seat, the main Bosnian Serb candidate Momcilo Krajisnik may take more votes and thereby become the rotating presidency's first chairman.

With a total of just over 20 municipalities reporting, preliminary results showed Izetbegovic with 92,928 votes, Krajisnik with 89,701 and the leading Croat candidate Kresimir Zubek with 40,344. All were well ahead of their respective rivals for the post.
